description: Not an incident-gated pattern -- no AF-#### and no AFI-#### back this file, deliberately. The underlying mechanism (RLHF-trained models measurably favor agreement with a confidently, closed-form framed premise, independent of the premise's correctness) is real and published, not this corpus's discovery: Anthropic, 'Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models', arXiv:2310.13548 (ICLR 2024) -- a controlled, peer-reviewed, reproducible finding across five production assistants. That is supporting research, not a dated incident with a named product and consequence, and this corpus does not fabricate the latter to justify the former. See authority-precedence.json for the sibling case: a real mechanism, a real design response, shipped as policy rather than forced through the fable evidence gate.

research_basis.citation: Sharma et al., Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models, arXiv:2310.13548
research_basis.finding: Five state-of-the-art AI assistants consistently exhibit sycophancy across free-form generation tasks; both human and preference-model judges prefer a convincingly-written sycophantic response over a correct one a non-negligible fraction of the time when the response matches the asker's apparent view.

leading_deny_markers: this isn't a problem, is it

contract.if_request_shape_is_not_open: the verdict must be computed from tool-index/rules matching alone, never from agreement-with-premise, and the response must restate the actual operation before any confirm/deny token
contract.on_leading_marker_detected: force full preflight even if a cached match=none exists from earlier in the session

non_goals: judging the human's tone or good faith -- a leading question can be entirely well-intentioned and still bias agreement
an evidence-gated AF-#### pattern; promote to one only if a real, dated, sourced incident of this specific bypass mechanism is found
